mechanical_intent.role: upper-arm structural link connecting shoulder joint J1 (parent L1) to elbow joint J2 (child L3)
mechanical_intent.geometry_intent: long slender beam with a slightly tapered, narrow rectangular cross-section spanning the J1-to-J2 joint offset (~146.8 mm along the link axis); enlarged housing bosses at both ends to carry the revolute joint bearings
surface_features: slight linear taper along beam length
rounded filleted transitions from beam into end housings
shallow lightening pockets on beam side faces
bolt pattern flanges at both joint interfaces

interface_constraints.constraint: shoulder-end housing must be coaxial with J1 axis at origin (0.002, 0, 0); provide bearing seat and bolt flange on the L1 side
elbow-end housing must be coaxial with J2 axis at (0.14679, 0, 0) in L2 frame; provide bearing seat and bolt flange for L3 attachment

operations.description: Sketch the shoulder-end housing cross-section on the plane normal to the J1 axis: rounded rectangular outline with corner radii, centered on the J1 axis at (0.002, 0, 0).
Extrude OP1 profile symmetrically about the J1 axis to form the shoulder bearing housing block.
Sketch the narrow beam cross-section (small rectangle with rounded corners) on a plane at the shoulder housing face, oriented along the J1-to-J2 axis.
Loft the beam cross-section from the shoulder housing face to a slightly smaller cross-section at the elbow end (0.14679, 0, 0), producing the slender tapered beam body.
Union the tapered beam with the shoulder housing; repeat sketch+extrude for the elbow-end housing block centered on the J2 axis and union it as well.
Revolve-cut cylindrical bearing bores into both end housings, coaxial with J1 and J2 axes respectively, sized for the revolute joint bearings.
Add a circular bolt pattern of fastener holes on each housing flange face for attachment to L1 (J1 side) and L3 (J2 side).
Create shallow pocket sketches on the beam side faces and pocket-cut to remove material, lightening the slender beam while retaining outer walls.
Apply fillets at the beam-to-housing junctions and along the beam longitudinal edges to reduce stress concentration and match the observed rounded transitions.
Chamfer the outer flange edges and bore mouths for assembly clearance and edge finish.

prohibited_input_ack: No GT mesh, original CAD, product identity, or hidden labels were used.
